articles.title: Pokopia Pokédex review: a classic, reimagined
articles.summary: Pokémon Pokopia’s new Pokédex beefs up the original model with a host of fresh features perfect for 2026.
articles.body: Thirty years ago, Nintendo struck gold with the release of the original Pokémon games. Soon, kids across the world were introduced to dozens of magical creatures that they could befriend and learn more about using sophisticated electronic encyclopedias known as Pokédexes. The first Pokédexes were reflections of how the Pokémon world was shaped by advanced technology. And with each subsequent generation, Pokédexes evolved; by 2019 they stopped being dedicated devices and became applications on phones powered by disembodied spirits. Rotom Phones could do more things than their predecessors, but many players have continued to think of the handhelds as Pokédexes because that’s their primary function. And that nostalgia is part of what led to Nintendo releasing its latest (fictional) pocket-sized smart device. Rather than debuting a new generation of Rotom Phone, Pokopia introduces an updated version of the original ’Dex that has been tricked out with a bevy of thoughtful updates. The new clamshell might look like an antique when you first get it into your hands, but when you start using it, you can see that Nintendo and its collaborators — The Pokémon Company, Game Freak, and Omega Force — have engineered this device with the present day in mind. [Product: Pokopia Pokédex | Unlike the past few Rotom Phones, which took cues from modern smartphones, the new Pokédex goes back to the basics with a focus on identifying wild monsters and explaining interesting things about them. Aesthetically, the device is very much a throwback to the Kanto days with its small screens, durable hinge, and array of physical buttons. But once you power this Pokédex on and begin tinkering with its applications, it becomes clear how much more full-featured it is compared to the original. One of the bigger changes here is the addition of new front- and back-facing camera arrays that can be used to take selfies and photos of pokémon you encounter in Pokopia’s various biomes. In addition to alerting you when a photo-worthy moment is happening nearby, the camera’s object recognition functionality can also be used to identify items you find while out exploring. And if you connect your Pokédex to a Pokémon Center’s 3D printer, images you upload can be used to generate physical copies of useful tools, furniture, and even plants. The camera’s image quality is great, but you might find yourself frustrated by the Pokédex’s minuscule internal storage that limits you to saving up to 80 images as “memories” and an additional 20 as references for the 3D printer. Curiously, this Pokédex can wirelessly receive video calls from Pokémon Center PC users, but it doesn’t allow you to send any sort of outgoing messages from your end. Depending on how you look at it, this detail can be either an annoying bug or a feature that encourages you to interact with people face-to-face, but either way, the Pokédex boasted strong call quality in our experience. [Image: [Image: [Image: Because Pokopia tasks you with building suitable environments for different types of pokémon, the new Pokédex also features a sizable index of habitats with entries that detail all of the things you need in order to attract specific monsters. Though it can be tedious constantly referring to the Habitat Dex to make sure that you’ve arranged things just right to lure your target pokémon, the feature is a marked improvement — in terms of having fun — over previous Pokédexes, which could only tell you the general locations where a monster might appear. The Habitat Dex feels like a reminder that your main goal in Pokopia is to build relationships with pokémon as you restore the ruined world around you. It’s a charming riff on a classic element of the Pokémon franchise, but the Pokédex starts to feel weird when you fire up its most surprising app. Pokopia involves a lot of you waiting around for pokémon to show up, which seems to be the reason why you can purchase security cameras from the Pokémon Centers. Once you place them on the ground, multiple cameras can remotely connect to your Pokédex and provide you with a live feed of whatever is happening around them. [Image: [Image: This makes it very easy to check in and see if a pokémon has appeared in one location while you’re off somewhere else handling other tasks. But the cameras — which you can direct to turn around via your Pokédex — bring an element of Ring-like surveillance to Pokopia that feels somewhat morally dubious when you consider that the game’s pokémon are meant to be your friends and neighbors, not pets. Because the new Pokédex isn’t possessed by a Rotom, it’s not quite as versatile or flashy as the smart gadgets Nintendo has gotten into the habit of iterating on lately. But that simplicity is ideal for a slow, relaxing life sim like Pokopia. And the device’s timeless design makes it a solid addition to the franchise’s tech history.

articles.title: Vibe-Coded Mashup Mods Have Taken Over X This Week
articles.summary: I have spent the last three days scrolling through some of the most insane mod videos I've ever seen. Modders are taking games that have been decompiled with Claude, and mashing them up with other games. As the week has gone on, there have only been more clips of these mods pouring out on X/Twitter.
articles.body:
I have spent the last three days scrolling through some of the most insane mod videos I've ever seen. Modders are taking games that have been decompiled with Claude, and mashing them up with other games. As the week has gone on, there have only been more clips of these mods pouring out on X/Twitter.

One person created a mashup of World of Warcraft and Call of Duty: World at War ; another combined Escape From Tarkov with Skyrim . There’s even one that takes Insomniac’s Spider-Man and combines it with Batman Arkham City , where the player is able to swing around Batman’s turf.

These mods are everywhere online right now, though they thankfully haven’t filtered into modding websites like Nexus Mods yet. But, with the sheer volume of these mods and with how accessible Opus 5.5 is, it feels like it’s only a matter of time before the gates are fully torn down. And if that happens, it could change the face of the modding scene entirely.

Claude Opus 5.5 launched last week, promising cheaper tokens and more efficient code work. I'm sure that Anthropic meant for it to be used by professionals, but gamers have used it to create some of the weirdest mods I have ever seen.

Opus is a model that can power AI agents, which can be deployed to create entire games from the engine, to the art and enemy behavior. Brendan Jowett has a great video on YouTube of the model in action: He develops little slices of video games and compares them directly with the same tasks from OpenAI’s Astra 6 model. While the results of both are far from what you’d expect from a fully featured game, Claude’s new model has clearly come a long way.

The problem with the examples in Jowett’s video is that while the models are good at piecing together disparate parts of a game, enemy AI (lol) and art assets are lackluster to say the least. In one of the slices, a space combat sim, the space fighter flys at a diagonal angle, while moving in a straight line ahead, and shooting. In another slice enemies completely ignore the player character.

As good as Claude Opus 5.5 seems to be, it’s still lightyears away from developing something like a true mashup of Minecraft and Elden Ring from scratch. But the model doesn’t have to start from scratch.

The big, driving force behind a lot of these mods is decompilation, where people are pointing Opus at a game and letting the agent break it down to its source code (here’s a handy blog if you want to really get in the weeds). Just earlier today, we covered Halo: Combat Evolved being decompiled and ported to run natively in a browser . Once that step is complete, it takes little effort to take that source code and work huge swaths of games into other games as mods, and with very little input from the user.

Couple that with the relatively affordable tokens, and it shouldn’t be surprising that X/Twitter’s generally pro-AI users went wild with it, creating hundreds of mashups. And it doesn’t seem like it’s slowing down any time soon; what started off as a weird video that my boss sent me on Tuesday has now evolved to the point where I can’t even open X/Twitter without seeing a deluge of these mods.

The obvious problem with all of this is that these models are breaking open games developed by real people, getting the source code and then just mashing stuff together without consideration or permission from the original developers. That’s nothing particularly new – the modding scene is definitely no stranger to mashups, all the Thomas the Tank Engine mods are proof of that. However, this trend might be breaking into new territory, thanks to decompilation.

This could be another reason none of these mods have made their way onto any distribution platforms. Nexus Mods doesn’t outright ban AI-generated content, but it doesn’t let people use AI tools to upload content that they don’t have the rights to.

In a blog post from 2023, Nexus laid out its rules around AI generated content. The policy states that , “In order to prevent any issues with your mods, we encourage you to avoid using these tools unless you have explicit permission to use all the assets. This is particularly true for AI-generated voice acting but also covers images, models, code and anything else that you can use this technology to create.”

Every single one of these passthrough mods are using images, models, and code that the people generating them don’t have the rights to. But it’s only a matter of time until some platform holder allows these mods to be hosted, and I’m sure a massive legal battle will happen immediately afterwards.

Way before all of these Claude-authored mod videos started cropping up online, people had been creating mods by hand for years, typically out of pure love for the game. It shouldn’t be surprising, then, that a lot of mod authors aren’t fans of this phenomenon.

Mod authors have been expressing their frustration on X/Twitter as this has been happening. “I mod games and I'm not shy about the fact that I use AI to do it. I hate this bullshit ‘trend’. Pure slop, there's nothing creative about this at all,” kran27_ posted. “AI has a lot of potential in the modding scene, but the shit that's getting the clicks is this jingling keys bullshit.”

Kran wasn’t alone, with discountmodder ready to just leave the scene, saying, “Dude I'm really disappointed. If this becomes the permanent state of modding, this may be my last project. I don't wanna be involved in an AI slop-factory.”

I can’t escape the feeling that most of these mashups are born from people just playing with a new AI model and seeing what will happen, and I hope that this weird trend will die off soon. Modding is one of the best parts of PC gaming, and there is a lot of incredible content that people make just because they love a game. Some of the best games started off as mods, after all, and without them we never would have got the likes of Half-Life or League of Legends.

I hope that this is just a trend, rather than a sign of where the modding scene is heading. Fortunately, because these mods seemingly only exist to farm engagement on Twitter (at least so far), you don’t have to worry too much about them if you just want to start a new modded run of The Witcher 3 Remastered. If anything, it just means that if you want to avoid AI content, you need to pay even more attention to who you’re getting your mods from.

Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

articles.title: Lanterns: Who Killed Hal Jordan and More of Our Biggest Questions Heading Into the Finale
articles.summary: Who killed Hal Jordan? Is Hal Jordan even dead!? What's up with Sinestro and that planet? We have so many questions heading into the Lanterns season finale...
articles.body:
Spoilers follow for Lanterns Episodes 1-7.

Lanterns, am I right? While the HBO series set in James Gunn’s DC Universe was divisive among some fans at the outset – what with the whole killing off Hal Jordan in the first episode situation – it has become increasingly buzzy with each passing week, with showrunner Chris Mundy and his fellow creators Damon Lindelof and Tom King building mystery upon mystery over the course of the first season.

And now, as we head into the season finale this weekend, there are a ton of questions that need to be answered. We’re breaking down the biggest ones we have right here, but please comment below and let us know what other questions you might have regarding Lanterns Season 1… and the possible answers and theories you have as well!

Assuming, of course, Hal (Kyle Chandler) even is dead (see below for more on that), there are obviously several possibilities as to who could’ve put a bullet in the ex-Green Lantern’s head in the 2026 time period. The chief suspects seem to be:

Taking these one at a time, it seems pretty unlikely that John (Aaron Pierre) would’ve killed Hal. For starters, he’s one of our two lead characters, and while both of these Lanterns can be sort of assholes – especially to each other – they’re still ultimately meant to be figures who we sympathize with and want to cheer on. But even beyond that, it doesn’t make much story sense for John to have done this; he essentially already “beat” Hal during the events of Episode 5 , leaving him a broken man without the ring and only the consequences of his own actions left to face up to. By the time we catch up with John, now an architect and businessman, in 2026, he clearly still harbors a lot of feelings about his past as a Lantern, but needing to kill Hal is not one of them.

Kerry (Kelly Macdonald) on the other hand, well… as much as we love her, the good sheriff has been known to keep secrets from our heroes in the past. And while I buy that she and the post-prison, repentant Hal had a thing going, as well as that she is truly gutted by his death, that doesn’t mean that their relationship would’ve kept her from doing the deed if it was necessary for a greater cause. Let’s not forget, Kerry was saved by Zoe Macon the Manhunter (Poorna Jagannathan) back when she first arrived in Rushville while on the run from Gotham City. And it was during that encounter that she essentially swore her allegiance to Zoe. So if there is still some contingency plan in place for Zoe, even though John killed the Manhunter in 2016, there’s every reason to believe that Kerry would still be instrumental in keeping that plan on track…

Which brings us to Kerry’s son, Noah (Shea Pritchard). There sure seems to be something fishy with this kid – the dude went and copped out on the college hat ceremony after the whole town showed up for it with bated breath! He also, you know, had a grandmother (step-grandmother, but still) who was a Manhunter. We’ll talk more about him below, but he’s high on the list of suspects.

Look, Kerry told John how, after he got out of prison, Hal was on a relentless mission in Rushville to make up for the disastrous events that landed him behind bars in the first place, knocking on doors and offering his help and such. Is it out of the realm of possibility to think that in order to keep the town safe this time – or maybe even to make up for what happened to the town 10 years ago in 2016 – that he would take his own life if need be?

I’ve already talked about this before , but it’s very much not out of the realm of possibility that Hal isn’t even dead. Maybe he’s just “dead-ish” even? We already know that the show is full of aliens who walk around posing as humans, which means that the body we’ve seen could just be an alien that took Hal’s form. It’s also possible that Hal is regenerating from the wounds that killed him. Yes, it’s a crazy sci-fi concept, but John previously got a total skin graft after Zoe let him burn in that car fire and, as many eagle-eyed fans have pointed out, the trailer for the season finale shows a similar circular mark on Hal’s inner arm that John had after that Manhunter Miracle Medicine. Zoe explained to John that basically her tech required a skin sample (pulled from that spot on his arm) in order to repair/replace his burned skin, so perhaps the same methodology is being used to fix Hal… albeit it would have to unscramble his shot-up brains in this case. Or maybe the dead body was just a clone spawned from that same technology?

Why Can John Stewart Create Constructs Without the Ring?

Remember in Episode 2 when John tried to fly, but instead he created a cute little green bird construct? And the bird still existed and followed him around, even when he didn’t have the ring on? This was the first – but not last – indication that John has some kind of, well, super superpower that other Green Lanterns don’t. The Halogram is very impressed by this ability in Episode 7 , when John summons him without the ring, saying “Bravo… it’s goddamned incredible!” It’s nice to get compliments from your seemingly dead mentor’s hologram.

But that still doesn’t answer how he’s able to do it. Presumably, John’s extraordinary ability to Green Lantern without a Green Lantern ring is tied to his extreme potential and the frankly insane training during his childhood by his we-need-a-new-word-for-helicopter-parents parents. Don’t forget, Sinestro (Ulrich Thomsen) told Hal from Space Azkaban that the second greatest threat Hal was facing was the Manhunter, with the implication being that the greatest threat was John. And what could be more powerful than a Green Lantern who doesn’t need the ring… or the Guardians for that matter?

Again, this perfect Rushville all-state quarterback has got to have something going on beyond being a perfect Rushville all-state quarterback. The hat ceremony thing, which I previously mentioned, was just weird (and also rude), but also, with such a short season, why would the show’s writers introduce the aged-up version of Noah in Episode 6 if he wasn’t going to be important in some way? In Episode 5, his step-grandmother/Manhunter Zoe tells the young Noah (Cary Christopher) to remember what she taught him… and that’s the same episode where everything goes to hell in a handbasket in town. We know Zoe meticulously planned her own protection by essentially drafting half the town to work for her, including Noah’s mom, so it only makes sense that she would have Tony Soprano/Batman-style contingency plans upon plans upon plans, including what would happen if she was killed. But then again, are we sure it was even Zoe who actually died in Episode 5? Could Noah be Zoe!?

What’s the Deal With Sinestro on That Dead Planet?

Man, speaking of really holding your fire until the end of a short season. Sinestro, discussed here or there and seen briefly in Episodes 2 and 4, finally shows up at the end of Episode 7, seemingly stranded on the dead world that John and the Halogram have traveled to via portal… but apparently meant to be an important part of the season finale. Guy Gardner (Nathan Fillion) had previously said that someone broke Sinestro out of the Guardians’ prison, and that Hal was a likely suspect if not for the fact that he was also in (Earth) prison. (And by the way, the timeline here is a little wonky because Guy tells John this info in an almost whispery, gossipy way, as if it’s breaking news, but meanwhile we know Hal has been out of prison for about a year – and is believed to be dead – at that point. Which would mean Sinestro must’ve broken out of Space Azkaban at least a year ago.)

So how does Sinestro popping up on that alien planet connect to everything? This is the same world that Antaan (Paul Ben-Victor) and his people hailed from, a race that was virtually wiped out by the Manhunters. It’s also the world that Hal left a portal to in his storage unit, which he apparently wanted John to find. Did Hal want Sinestro and John to team up for some reason? Neither is a particular fan of the Guardians, so could Hal perhaps be orchestrating some kind of Oan revolution from beyond the grave… one last “f you” to the powers that be?

What Did Kerry Get Up to in Gotham That Was So Bad?

We saw in flashback how Kerry would’ve been killed by a pair of scary dudes who had tracked her from Gotham City to Rushville, if not for the timely intervention of Zoe. After being saved by Zoe, she essentially began a new life in the town and eventually became sheriff (and a secret surrogate of Zoe’s). As IGN’s Jesse Schedeen has previously pointed out, Kerry’s name is also a big Batman clue : the Kane family are related to Bruce Wayne, as Martha Wayne was originally Martha Kane. Kathy Kane and Kate Kane, depending on when you were reading comics or watching CW shows, were both also Batwoman. So assuming the name of this character is not an accident – and not much on this show is – we’ve gotta wonder how a high-falutin’ member of the Kane family could fall in with such a rough element that she would’ve been killed if not for a Manhunter. It seems unlikely that Lanterns Season 1 will have time to dig further into this topic, but if the show moves forward with a Season 2, perhaps we’ll learn more about Kerry’s history… and maybe even any rich, famous, orphaned, dressed-in-black cousins she might have back home?

Remind Me: What Exactly Has Been the Order of Succession for Earth’s Green Lanterns?

This one’s easy! In 1986, Abin Sur crashed on Earth, and his ring almost went to John Stewart’s father, but Stewart Sr. couldn’t cut it, so instead Hal Jordan inherited the Green Lantern mantle. Hal was Earth’s Lantern for the next 20 years, until the disaster in Rushville when John took the ring from him. But he rejected the Guardians’ offer to become the new Green Lantern. It was around this same time that the gym teacher named Guy Gardner became the new Green Lantern, and continues to be through 2026. (Also, for comics fans, it seems that Alan Scott – the Golden Age Green Lantern – never took the mantle… in this timeline anyway.)

What questions do you have heading into the Lanterns finale? Let’s discuss below!

Talk to Scott Collura @scottcollura.bsky.social , or listen to his Star Trek podcast, Transporter Room 3 . Or do both!

articles.title: Disney Says Conversations About Buying Epic Games Are Not Happening 'Right Now'
articles.summary: Disney has responded after rumors suggested it was interested in buying Fortnite developer Epic Games.
articles.body:
Disney has responded after rumors suggested it was interested in buying Fortnite developer Epic Games.

Disney president and chief creative officer Dana Walden touched on the company's relationship with Epic during an interview with Bloomberg Live . When asked if there have been talks about expanding their previously established relationship with a full-on acquisition, she said that strategy isn't something Disney is entertaining, at least right now.

"Well, I think that it was pretty obvious that we had very serious conversations about an investment and an equity stake," Walden responded. "Those are not the conversations we're having right now, but we have a great partnership and a number of launches coming up over the next two years that are going to demonstrate the value of this partnership."

The relationship referenced here was solidified when Disney announced it acquired a $1.5 billion stake in Epic back in early 2024. It was a massive play that it promised would result in collaborations across Fortnite and more in the future.

"Our exciting new relationship with Epic Games will bring together Disney’s beloved brands and franchises with the hugely popular Fortnite in a transformational new games and entertainment universe," then-CEO Bob Iger said. "This marks Disney’s biggest entry ever into the world of games and offers significant opportunities for growth and expansion. We can’t wait for fans to experience the Disney stories and worlds they love in groundbreaking new ways."

We're still feeling the shockwaves of that deal, but some suspected it could evolve into more than a simple partnership. Tech reporter Alex Heath said in March 2026 that some Disney executives were "waiting for that moment" to go all in on an acquisition . Then, in April, Bloomberg reported that Epic was working on an extraction shooter featuring Disney characters with plans to launch in November 2026.

Fortnite x Star Wars New Games and Rewards

We're now kicking off October with no official mention of that unannounced project, but that doesn't mean Disney x Epic is going anywhere any time soon. While an acquisition isn't in the cards, Walden's promise regarding "a number of launches" set to arrive in the next few years suggests there is plenty more to talk about.

We'll have to wait and see how the two entertainment giants work together moving forward. In the meantime, you can read some of the other ways Disney and Epic have bolstered their relationship, including a Disneyland-exclusive Fortnite skin and officially licensed Star Wars minigames .

articles.title: Former NFL Coach Mike Tomlin Is a Hardcore Minecraft Player, Reveals City He Took 12 Years to Build
articles.summary: Former NFL coach Mike Tomlin spent 19 seasons with the Pittsburgh Steelers and won Super Bowl LXIII, and now he's added another major accomplishment to his resume: becoming a Minecraft YouTuber.
articles.body:
Former NFL coach Mike Tomlin spent 19 seasons with the Pittsburgh Steelers and won Super Bowl LXIII, and now he's added another major accomplishment to his resume: becoming a Minecraft YouTuber.

The former coach gave football fans a little something different when he launched his new YouTube channel earlier this week. With a profile picture taken in front of NBC's Football Night in America logo, watchers probably weren't expecting Tomlin's first upload to see him confess how his love for architecture and family led him to work on a Minecraft city he spent 12 years building.

"You know, 12 or 13 years ago, when my kids were in middle school, they'd be in their room all weekend and have friends over. They were obsessed with playing this game, Minecraft, that I knew nothing about," he explained as his son and channel operator, Dino, sat in the background. "I got interested because I just was mesmerized by what could occupy their attention for such large periods of time."

He admitted he lacked the "stick control" to handle something like Minecraft's Survival mode but still managed to find enjoyment in Creative Mode. That's where Mojang's systems really started to click.

"I like to build," he said. "I've always had an interest in architecture, and so forth, so I started doing this creative city. It was a means of spending time with them. They participated all over this city. All my kids have buildings."

However, as his kids went off to high school and college, their interest in Minecraft waned. For Tomlin, it was just beginning. In 2026, after 12 years of building, the sandbox phenomenon has become therapeutic for the former NFL coach, and what he's built has the internet in disbelief.

"This is where it all started for me," Tomlin said as a blocky blue pond surrounded by detailed city buildings faded into view. His tour then begins with a closer look at a hotel. This one building features a fully fleshed-out interior with labeled rooms, a lobby, a ballroom, a pool, bathrooms, and more. Tomlin even factored in how lighting might affect the views in some of these rooms – and that's just one of many locations he's made.

"I was always inspired," he added. "I'd go places, and I'd see things and buildings, and I get inspired, I go home, and I work on it."

articles.title: Capcom Announces Plans to Transform the RE Engine Into an AI-Generation Game Engine — ‘Our Goal Is a Future Where We Create Games Together With AI’
articles.summary: Resident Evil and Street Fighter developer Capcom revealed some big changes coming to its RE Engine, which they plan to gradually improve and transform into an "AI-generation game engine."
articles.body:
Resident Evil and Street Fighter developer Capcom revealed some big changes coming to its RE Engine, which they plan to incrementally improve and transform into an "AI-generation game engine."

On October 2, Capcom held its own tech conference, called ‘Capcom Open Conference RE: 2026.’ One of the most notable takeaways from this event was a presentation given by programmer Satoshi Ishida, titled ‘The Outlook and Future of the REX Project, Further Evolving the RE Engine for the Next Generation.’ The purpose of this presentation was to outline several major changes coming to the RE Engine, which will come in the form of a multi-step improvement project called ‘REX.’

As reported by Japanese news outlet GameBiz , Ishida mentioned three major issues that Capcom is currently experiencing when it comes to game development: First, games are now so massive that simple processes have become extremely time-consuming; increased numbers of staff mean an engine is needed that’s easy for everyone to use; and finally, “successfully integrating AI technology into development workflows has become an essential condition for streamlining future development.”

Resident Evil Requiem – Performance Screenshots

GameBiz’s report confirmed that REX was created to help solve these problems by improving the efficiency of game development, game performance, tools, quality assurance, etc. Capcom felt that, rather than creating a brand-new engine from scratch, gradually adding these improvements over time is the best way to help evolve the RE Engine to the next generation.

We won’t get into the weeds of all the specific improvements included in the REX program, but Capcom is making at least some of them open-source for the purpose of training AI. Most interestingly, AI plays into Capcom’s larger, long-term goal of turning the RE Engine into an “AI-generation game engine” using its REX improvements.

GameBiz stated that REX unifies the entire RE Engine system under the “world’s most common programming language," meaning that it’s equal parts easier for humans to use and for AI to understand. Capcom’s goal is to build a future where it “creates games together with AI”; keeping REX in mind, this seems to mean that Capcom is utilizing artificial intelligence to speed up and streamline certain processes to make development easier, not necessarily to generate assets or artworks wholesale.

In the past, Capcom has been publicly averse to using AI to create assets , but confirmed that it will use artificial intelligence as a tool for optimizing how it makes games.

“We will not implement assets generated by AI into our games.” Capcom said in a March 2026 shareholders meeting. “However, we plan to proactively use it as a contributing technology to improve the efficiency and productivity of the game development process. To this end, we are currently exploring ways to implement it in various areas, including graphics, sound and programming."

This is the latest big news to come from Capcom after Resident Evil executive producer Jun Takeuchi revealed that plans are already in place to prepare the series for when RE remakes catch up to modern games, saying the series is being developed along “two tracks.”

It’s been a big year for the company; this year alone, Capcom has produced three critically-acclaimed titles in Resident Evil Requiem , Pragmata , and Onimusha: Way of the Sword , alongside two movie adaptations in Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil and Legendary’s Street Fighter flick, set to release in theaters on October 16, 2026.

articles.title: Love and Deepspace Devs Issue Warning to Players After Deadly Drink Recipes Go Viral
articles.summary: The official social media account for the popular RPG-dating sim Love and Deepspace issued a warning to players after announcing some fictional cocktails with potentially disastrous real-world consequences if actually consumed.
articles.body:
The official social media account for the popular RPG-dating sim Love and Deepspace issued a warning to players after announcing some fictional cocktails with potentially disastrous real-world consequences if actually consumed.

On September 28, Love and Deepspace revealed five ‘Shimmering Blend’ cocktail recipes as part of an in-game event, each themed around one of the game’s dashing romanceable characters. While they’re pretty to look at, you shouldn’t actually make some of these, as they include garnishes that are poisonous to humans.

For example, one of these drinks is made of pomegranate juice, with a garnish of cinnamon and datura. Another features sweet peach juice with a flame lily garnish and gelatin sheets.

There’s nothing wrong with peach and pomegranate juice, but these floral garnishes are making some players anxious that a fan might actually try to out the recipes themselves. Datura is a highly poisonous plant and is considered psychoactive ; when consumed, it produces side effects like delirium, fever, tachychardia, and hallucinations.

Flame Lilies are also dangerous, as all parts of the plant contain a chemical called colchicine; while it’s used for medicinal purposes, it can be lethal , causing symptoms like fever, vomiting, diarrhea, and even hypovolemic shock, which causes the loss of lethal amounts of blood and bodily fluids.

It didn’t take long for concerned fans to point out these dangerous plants, fearing that some players might try their hand at making the cocktails for real. Commenters flooded the replies with calls for the Love and Deepspace account to delete the post completely, with one writing , “Delete this. This is literal poison. Nobody make this.”

Safety Notice: All drinks shown are fictional and for in-game purposes only. Do not attempt to recreate or consume them in reality. — Love and Deepspace (@Love_Deepspace) September 30, 2026

Safety Notice: All drinks shown are fictional and for in-game purposes only. Do not attempt to recreate or consume them in reality.

“Hey, so some of these flowers are literally poisonous. Be careful. This is so reckless to post this,” another said .

"Don't try to recreate these drinks, they contain toxic plants!" yet another warned . "I can't believe this is posted as 'recipes.'"

Not long after, the LaDS account added a follow-up post with a safety notice, which reads: “All drinks shown are fictional and for in-game purposes only. Do not attempt to recreate or consume them in reality.”

Fan Tribute to Love and Deepspace's Valko

In addition to calls from fans to delete the posts, the LaDS social media accounts continue to be flooded with photos of canceled love interest Valko , who was announced and subsequently canned before he was even released. This prompted an impressive movement from the game’s playerbase, who created shrines to the character and even gathered outside the developer’s physical offices to make their voices heard.

articles.title: Valkyries coach Nakase goes down on sideline late in Golden State's playoff-clinching win over Wings
articles.summary: SAN FRANCISCO (AP) — Golden State Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase went down to her knees with her head and hands on the court near the team's bench with 1:40...
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO (AP) — Golden State Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase went down to her knees with her head and hands on the court near the team's bench with 1:40 left in a scary moment late in a 77-73 series-winning victory over the Dallas Wings on Friday night.

Nakase was helped up by athletic trainer Katelin Knox. She finished the game but exited the floor immediately following the final escorted by a member of her staff after the final buzzer, with her team celebrating at midcourt.

The team said she was feeling fine afterward, but assistant coach Kasib Powell addressed the media in a postgame news conference where she typically speaks.

"Natalie's fine, obviously it's a quick turnaround, we play again on Sunday. She wouldn't miss it for anything," Powell said, adding: "It's still new to us, we're just trying to figure it out. We just know that we (saw) her afterward and she was fine, laughing, in great spirits. We'll figure out more as we go but I think she's totally fine, she's talking, she's laughing in the back. We look forward to preparing and getting ready for Sunday."

The Valkyries will host the defending champion Las Vegas Aces for Game 1 in the best-of-five semifinals.

"She's OK, she's fine," guard Gabby Williams said. "We just tried to step up ourselves. We're just happy that she's OK."

Golden State rallied from 16 points down to eliminate the Wings in the deciding Game 3 at Chase Center. The 46-year-old Nakase guided the Valkyries to a history-making 2025 season as the first expansion team to make the playoffs in its inaugural season.

Guard Tiffany Hayes said she didn't see Nakase go down, then the coach was right back at it — even successfully winning a challenge.

"Didn't miss a beat," Powell said. "We were locked in as that happened, when she went to the sidelines she drew the next play up, she was in the huddle getting on them about getting a stop, so she didn't skip a beat at all."

Powell added that the Valkyries kept their composure "and just rally around each other and her."

"We do know that she will be ready for Sunday," Powell said.

articles.title: Carrie, Avatar, and More of the Most Anticipated Movies and TV Shows to Stream in October
articles.summary: From yet another Mike Flanagan adaptation of a Stephen King story to a Friday the 13th prequel series and the Season 1 finale of Lanterns, here are our picks for what to stream this month.
articles.body:
October is finally here to bring spooky season to the world — please ignore the Christmas decorations already on display at your local pharmacy — and that means plenty of terrifying television coming to your screen this month as well!

Don’t worry; it’s not all scares and screams, as we’ve also got some highly anticipated drama debuts, the finale of one of the most discussed superhero series in recent years, the debut of what looks to be one of the other most discussed superhero series in recent years, and much more.

So without further delay, let’s get into our list of 10 picks for movies and TV shows we can’t wait to stream this month. There’s so much good stuff, it’s… scary!

(Note: This list is presented in release date order.)

While MCU fans will probably be thrilled to see Black Widow (Florence Pugh) and the new Professor X (Christopher Abbott) play opposite each other, and costume drama aficionados are feasting with this latest sumptuous literary adaptation (John Steinbeck this time), the real story of Netflix’s East of Eden is behind the scenes.

That’s because it’s created by Zoe Kazan, who you might know from her on-screen work in everything from Revolutionary Road (2008) to The Big Sick (2017). With this series, she steps into the writer’s chair — all eight episodes were written or co-written by Kazan —and provides her own adaptation of the same work her grandfather Elia Kazan famously directed in 1955.

How will Kazan update or change things? You’ll have to watch for yourself to find out. But if you’re curious about the premise, the show follows the interwoven stories of two families over the decades. Steinbeck, who also wrote Of Mice and Men and the Pulitzer Prize-winning The Grapes of Wrath, considered this his greatest work. Clearly, Netflix has a lot of faith in the Kazan version: They’ve already put her in charge of a reboot of Lonesome Dove.

What shenanigans will brothers John Lantern (Aaron Pierre) and Hal Lantern (Kyle Chandler) get into in the final episode of the HBO series? Will they switch places to get John’s parents back together, or will their buddy Sinestro (Ulrich Thomsen) finally get what he deserves in front of the whole school?

We kid, but only because as of this writing, the HBO series has built up steam at a fever pitch with a time jump to the modern day, a ton of DCU references and easter eggs, searing lead performances by Pierre and Chandler, and consuming cultural conversation that’s the perfect Venn diagram of comic book and HBO Sunday Night Mystery fans.

The biggest question going into the finale isn’t any of the ongoing mysteries, but A), whether the excellently crafted Green Lantern series can stick the landing, and B), how much (if at all) it will set up Man of Tomorrow as well as a second season of the series. The other big question: Are you afraid?

Carrie, the new adaptation of the iconic Stephen King novel by TV’s horror maestro Mike Flanagan, is not what you think. To say more is to risk spoilers, but one aspect of the eight-episode Prime Video series we can talk about is that the show is set in the modern day, which changes things significantly.

When the telekinetic Carrie White’s (Summer H. Howell) father dies, she’s taken from home-schooling to high school. In 2026, that means social media, cell phones, school shooter drills — all the things that 1976 Carrie didn’t need to deal with, and 2013 Carrie only tangentially addressed. While you will see all the scenes you expect, from the “plug it up” scene in the shower to the iconic prom disaster, other things go in some jaw-dropping directions, from Margaret White (Samantha Sloyan) becoming an influencer to a fair amount of sympathy for teen bully Chris Hargensen (Alison Thorton).

We may not have needed another adaptation of King’s novel after four (!!!) previous movies and a stage musical, but this Carrie is relevant, surprising, has a huge twist we won’t spoil, and is another TV winner for Flanagan, showing his move from Netflix to Amazon is off to a great start.

The Josh Hartnettaissance continues with Netflix’s new six-episode series, which finds a small town besieged by a seeming sea monster. While it might seem like this is biting onto Widow’s Bay fever — small town, monsters, quirky — this was filmed last year, way before the Apple TV Emmy dominator was even on the radar. Based on trailers at least, Below also looks much more serious, and more in the vein of a supernatural Jaws.

Alongside Hartnett as a fisherman trying to save the Newfoundland town of Snook’s Arm, the cast also includes Mackenzie Davis, Charlie Heaton, and for a bit of Species vibes, Natasha Henstridge. Early reviews out of TIFF, where the pilot screened, are exceptionally positive, noting that while the show does play to some clichés, it’s gorgeously filmed and supremely gory.

Speaking of great casts, Ben Affleck is putting a team together for his new Netflix crime thriller, which finds the director/co-writer/star taking on the role of a mayoral candidate named Mark Kimball whose son is kidnapped. He and his wife (Kerry Washington) have mere hours to get the money to save their son’s life, with the unfortunate additional note that all their money is tied up in Kimball’s campaign. The movie also stars Gillian Anderson, Steven Yeun, and more, so you know it’s going to be extremely watchable at the very least.

As a director, Affleck hasn’t crushed it every time, but from the Oscar-winning Argo to the surprisingly engaging sneakers drama, Air, if you’ve got an Affleck movie that starts with the letter “A,” you’ve got a better than average chance it’ll earn an “A” from critics as well.

Where to start with this new animated Paramount+ series? It’s the third show in the Avatar: The Last Airbender franchise, and the first since The Legend of Korra completed its run in 2014. In the intervening time, there’s been a lot of behind-the-scenes controversy generated by the live-action series on Netflix and the stumbling release of the sequel movie Avatar Aang (though thankfully that turned out to be pretty good ).

Seven Havens takes place after Korra (Janet Varney) did something very bad; now everyone hates the Avatar. Enter Pavi (Saheli Kahn), a young Earthbender who finds out she’s the next Avatar — the one who can control all four elements (earth, air, fire, water). She’s also got a twin sister Nisha, and together they may be able to save the Seven Havens, which is all that’s left of civilization after whatever Korra did in the past.

With a new animation style and a seemingly darker tone than the franchise has had before, can Seven Havens succeed where other extensions of Avatar have… well, not failed , but definitely not gone as smoothly as one might have hoped? With 13 episodes in Season 1 and a second (and final) season already in the works, we’ll have plenty of time to find out.

The extraordinarily weird premise of Matchbox: The Movie, based on the Mattel toys of the same name, is that John Cena is a superspy reunited with his childhood friends when they’re drugged and kidnapped by a villainous group searching for a nuclear warhead. The rest of the gang — played by Jessica Biel, Sam Richardson, Arturo Castro, and Teyonah Parris — are all normal folks in over their heads, except for one crucial detail: They all played with Matchbox cars as kids. So the gang will use the skills they developed playing with tiny toy cars in their backyard to drive real cars, steal a nuclear warhead, and clear their names.

…Uh, what? In practice, the movie looks just like Fast and the Furious, but more comedic. Cena, at least, has a knack for choosing projects that show off his comedy chops in surprising ways; see the recent Coyote vs. Acme for one example. But — and we must repeat — what ? Not that this movie needed to have everyone shrinking down to drive toy cars, but the Matchbox connection seems as tangential as a bunch of folks who bought a zoo because they used to play Hungry Hungry Hippos.

The Barbie film (based on another Mattel property) worked because Greta Gerwig turned the lens back on the cultural impact of the iconic toy and used the premise to delve into our relationship with toys and the legacy of feminism in culture. Does anyone have the same relationship with Matchbox cars? And will the director of Extraction, Extraction 2, and Extraction 3 (Sam Hargrave) bring the same analytical lens to Matchbox that Gerwig did to Barbie and Ken? Vroom vroom — let’s drive on over to Apple TV to find out!

The modern MCU era of Marvel live-action TV began with WandaVision, and it sure looks like it’s going to end with VisionQuest, the third chapter after Agatha All Along. If so, things are going out with a bang. Taking over to finish out the trilogy is Terry Matalas of the superb 12 Monkeys series and the excellent third season of Star Trek: Picard; he’ll be bringing the new version of Vision (Paul Bettany) face to face with his somehow alive son Tommy (Ruaridh Mollica).

But the even more anticipated match-up is Vision and Ultron (James Spader), who’s back thanks to a group of marvelous AIs that Vision has stored in his head, including (all in human form) F.R.I.D.A.Y. (Orla Brady), E.D.I.T.H. (Emily Hampshire), J.A.R.V.I.S. (James D’Arcy), and more. They’re all hunted by the villainous Paladin (Todd Stashwick) and his associate, Philomena Cunk… sorry, actress Diane Morgan.

There’s lots going on here, but the MCU on Disney+ has always been at its best with shows like WandaVision and Agatha All Along, which feature great actors playing characters we love while fueling wild fan theories that invariably turn out not to be true… except when they do. We see the vision for this show; now it’s time to quest for answers.

The Young Jason Chronicles? The long-in-development Friday the 13th prequel series has seen an incredibly rocky road to screen, but now the A24 production is finally here — or almost here — on Peacock, with Linda Cardellini as Pamela Voorhees… aka the most murderous lunch lady known to screen.

Now helmed by showrunner Brad Caleb Kane — the singing voice of Aladdin ( look it up ) — who is making his name with prequel TV series about iconic movie monsters ( look IT up ), the show expands on the scant info we have about Pamela in the original slasher movies as well as opening up more about the town of Crystal Lake and the infamous camp that resides there. Plus, there are plenty of teases of game-changing mythology for the Friday the 13th franchise.

Is Friday the 13th on the same level as Nightmare on Elm Street or Halloween? Not really. So injecting any sort of sense into the nonsense could help flesh out the Jason Universe (no relation to Steven Universe). Add in Cardellini, who’s fresh off an Emmy win for DTF St. Louis, and you’ve got a meaty stew of ideas you’ll want to machete your way into.

Ever heard the tales of Baba Yaga, the witch who lives in a chicken house and steals children, and thought, “what if this was hella sexy?” Have we got the TV series for you! Premiering weekly on AMC+, Noah Reid stars as Rapp, a man investigating a disappearance in his small fishing town when he meets Katherine (Carrie Anne-Moss), a teacher who may or may not be Baba Yaga.

Also on the Canadian series is Heated Rivalry star Hudson Williams in not one but two roles, as well as other folks you will likely recognize from Canadian productions. Canada: It’s large, but there don’t seem to be a lot of actors!

Short version: If you want some blood sex magic with your witchy season (aka October), then Yaga might very well be your thing.

articles.title: 'I Did My Best' — Final Fantasy 7 Revelation Director Responds to Fans Asking for Full Disc Version
articles.summary: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation Naoki Hamaguchi said he did his best to fight for a disc release as the industry heads toward a "future where physical media is essentially disc-less."
articles.body:
Final Fantasy 7 Revelation Naoki Hamaguchi said he did his best to fight for a disc release as the industry heads toward a "future where physical media is essentially disc-less."

The lead developer in charge of next year's new remake chapter opened up about the state of gaming during an interview with Radio Times . It's a topic he's touched on before, but this time, he explained how his own appreciation for physical media led him to push for Final Fantasy 7 Revelation to get at least one disc as the industry speeds toward an all-digital future.

"Personally, obviously, I bought lots of physical editions of games as a child. Sometimes I buy digital editions of games, but if I'm particularly attached to a title, I want to get the physical version," Hamaguchi said, noting how the topic of a fully digital future has become "particularly sensitive" in recent months. "And you know, being in the industry, sometimes I want to get my friends or acquaintances who've worked on something to sign a copy of their own game."

Final Fantasy 7 Revelation is confirmed to have a disc option when it launches in 2027, but there are some caveats. When physical owners on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X, for example, pop their discs in, they should know the full experience will require an additional download – and a hefty one at that . It's a decision that has some fans split, but not one Hamaguchi and the team at Square Enix took lightly .

"I do really like and appreciate physical media," he said. "I see a lot of people on social media saying, 'No disc, no purchase,' and I understand where they're coming from."

Hamaguchi acknowledged that Final Fantasy 7 Revelation does have a disc alternative for those who want it, even if it's just a "key disc" that only has "the opening." He added that he understands that "there are people out there with a lot of opinions" about the future of physical media and shared a message to those who feel most passionately about the issue.

Final Fantasy 7 Revelation Preview Screenshots

"First of all, I've got people saying to me on social media, 'Give us a full disc version!' And so, from an overall perspective, let me first say that as the director, it's my responsibility to look after the content of the game to make sure it's fun, really exciting," he said. Then, smiling, he added, "The product line-up, the SKUs (stock keeping units), how it's going on sale; that is the responsibility of the publishing team. So, my authority there is somewhat limited."

Despite the "pressure" for disc-less editions and digital editions, Hamaguchi said he "used my position to put forth an argument for the physical version as much as possible." That resulted in negotiations, "both internally and with first parties," leading to Final Fantasy 7 Revelation's one-disc strategy. He added, "I completely understand there are those out there who may not really agree with that direction or approve of that direction," but it's what he fought for, and it's the best result he could conjure.

"I completely understand there are those out there who may not really agree with that direction or approve of that direction," he said. "But I would just say that I hope you understand that I completely see where you're coming from, and that I did my best."

He added with a laugh, "It is a very tricky subject."

Final Fantasy 7 Revelation will release with a disc when it releases for PC, Nintendo Switch 2, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S April 8, 2027. Although its launch strategy hasn't pleased everyone, it's a date that will see it arrive months before PlayStation phases out physical releases for new PS5 games . Even after Rockstar signaled changing times when it announced a disc-less release for Grand Theft Auto 6, Sony's decision sent shockwaves through the industry.

Gaming fans have expected an all-digital future to arrive at some point, but it seems to be here sooner than most expected. Elsewhere in the interview, Hamaguchi said he thinks "physical media will remain in some form going forward," but it's impossible to deny that change is coming.

"But the PC market, for example, is going from strength to strength, and lots of people already purchase digital copies of games and just download them.

"So, I can see a world in the not-too-distant future where physical media is essentially disc-less. You would have a copy of the code on a piece of paper inside the physical box or something like that."

For more on why the Square Enix team chose to approach Final Fantasy 7 Revelation's physical release the way it did, you can see Hamaguchi's explanation here . You can also read more about the director's love for physical media .

articles.title: Capcom is preparing for a ‘future where we create games together with AI’
articles.summary: During a presentation on the future of RE Engine, Capcom laid out its plans to embrace AI in ‘development workflows.’
articles.body: Capcom’s Pragmata might be all about the horrors of AI, but in practice the studio doesn’t seem so down on the tech. During the Capcom Open Conference RE: 2026 programmer Satoshi Ishida gave a presentation with the mouthful of a title: “The Outlook and Future of the REX Project, Further Evolving the RE Engine for the Next Generation.” During the talk he laid out the challenges facing studios producing games at the scale of Resident Evil, which can make even simple tasks extremely time consuming. The solution Ishida said is “successfully integrating AI technology into development workflows.” Capcom has said previously that it will not use AI-generated assets in its games, and instead would focus on using the tech to make development more efficient. Ishida’s comments seem to lineup, though definitely seem to leave the door open to more extensive use. He laid out a plan to turn RE Engine slowly, and incrementally, into an “AI-generation game engine” building towards a “a future where we create games together with AI,” according to IGN’s translation.

articles.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Video Reveals Major Change That Could End Wallhacks for Good
articles.summary: Wallhacks have plagued Call of Duty for years, but in Modern Warfare 4, Activision has a plan to change that.
articles.body:
Wallhacks have plagued Call of Duty for years, but in Modern Warfare 4 , Activision has a plan to change that.

If you're unfamiliar with the term, wallhacks are a type of cheat that allows nefarious players to see their opponents' every move through walls. Call of Duty is far from the only multiplayer-centric gaming franchise to suffer from cheaters who use the tool, but it might be the most infamous example – and in Modern Warfare 4, that's all about to change.

As detailed in a new video published on the franchise's official social media pages, publisher Activision and developer Infinity Ward revealed a new system aimed at combating wallhack cheaters. Called "server culling," the goal is to make Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 more reliable – and fair – than ever before.

Few things ruin a great match faster than wondering whether an opponent earned the win or saw you through a wall. Wallhacks give cheaters information they were never meant to have. With Modern Warfare 4, we’re introducing a new way to fight back: Server Culling. Here’s how it… pic.twitter.com/62m41zMbLa — Call of Duty (@CallofDuty) October 2, 2026

Few things ruin a great match faster than wondering whether an opponent earned the win or saw you through a wall. Wallhacks give cheaters information they were never meant to have. With Modern Warfare 4, we’re introducing a new way to fight back: Server Culling. Here’s how it… pic.twitter.com/62m41zMbLa

The relatively in-depth explanation touches on how cheaters have been able to use wallhacks thus far. Usually, servers share information, such as a player's in-game location, between game clients. It means that, even when you can't see an enemy hiding behind cover, waiting to pop out for an easy kill, the game itself still recognizes that the player is there.

Server culling, which saw Infinity Ward build occlusion layers into Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's environments, essentially limits information to what the player is able to see. So, if you can't see someone behind the wall, the backend can't either – and that goes for wallhackers, too.

"For legitimate players, the match plays exactly as intended," Activision explained. "For cheat developers, this creates a major new obstacle."

Server culling will touch every multiplayer map available in Modern Warfare 4 when launch arrives, but it doesn't stop there. Call of Duty's new take on DMZ, the Combat Outpost mode, Warzone, and future updates will benefit from this attack on wallhacks, too. All of this new tech works alongside pre-existing anti-cheat methods across all platforms , too.

Activision said it expects server culling to "disturb the cheat marketplace," but it won't "sit on our hands" when it comes to improving the overall experience going forward. There are plenty of different ways for cheaters to disrupt the experience for the average player, and while cheat manufacterers will no doubt look for new ways to learn from Activision's advancements, the publisher said it will do its best to stay on top of the issue.

"Cheat software can’t reveal information it never receives," the Call of Duty team explained in a follow-up post . "When a player shouldn’t be able to know where an opponent is, the server can now withhold that opponent’s location data from their hardware. It’s a new layer in the fight for fair play, working alongside the rest of our anti-cheat systems Server Culling will cover every map available at launch for MW4."

See you at launch, we'll keep at it — Call of Duty (@CallofDuty) October 2, 2026

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launches for PC, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S October 23, 2026. How fans will rank it amongst other installments in the franchise remains to be seen, but with changes to 2XP tokens and a villain played by Death Stranding and Casino Royale actor Mads Mikkelsen , it's clear the developers have put in the work to get players interested.

articles.title: Gears of War: E-Day Devs 'Proud to Be One of Xbox's Main Titles' Amid Newfound Focus on Exclusivity
articles.summary: The Gears of War: E-Day developers at The Coalition say they are "proud to be one of Xbox's main titles" as Microsoft refocuses on exclusivity.
articles.body:
The Gears of War: E-Day developers at The Coalition say they are "proud to be one of Xbox's main titles" as Microsoft refocuses on exclusivity.

Studio art director Aryan Hanbeck and creative director Matt Searcy opened up about The Coalition's place in the Xbox portfolio during an interview with gaming news content creator Destin Lergarie (via MP1st ). Searcy said he and the rest of the team were "proud" when asked how they feel about Gears of War: E-Day's status as an Xbox exclusive.

"Well, we feel great because Gears has such a long, storied… It's part of Xbox's DNA. It's woven into it," he said. "At The Coalition, we feel pretty honored to have Gears and be the ones bringing that legacy forward. We know how much it means to people. We know how much it means to us."

Gears of War: E-Day is firmly a console exclusive, but there was a lot of confusion surrounding which platforms Gears of War: E-Day would be available on as recently as four months ago. The once-Xbox-exclusive franchise made its debut on PlayStation consoles when original remaster, Gears of War: Reloaded, released in August 2025. Many took its presence on PS5 as a sign not only that the series would continue to come to Sony's console but also that the days of exclusive titles may nearly be behind us – and for a while, that seemed to be the case.

Leaked listings and rumors were officially shut down at the Xbox Games Showcase 2026 when Xbox CEO Asha Sharma proudly declared that Marcus Fenix and Dom Santiago's Emergence Day prequel story would only be coming to Xbox Series X/S and PC . It was a shock decision that arrived as the Microsoft gaming entity kicked off a broader push for more exclusive games . Perhaps even more shocking at the time were the announcements that immediately followed, including the company's promise to never release Xbox exclusive titles on rival platforms .

After leaked splash art fanned rumors that Xbox hastily decided to cancel a Gears of War: E-Day PS5 port, the company said it did not make any "last-minute" decisions when it comes to its platform choice. While Searcy said it brought The Coalition joy to see their new game leading Microsoft's renewed interest in exclusive titles, making sure they made a great game was what came first.

Gears of War: E-Day Gameplay Demo Reveal Xbox Games Showcase 2026 - Screenshots

"I think this is true of most game devs: You're just passionate about your craft," he said. "We're all gamers first and foremost. We love making games. We love making Gears. So, from our perspective, we just wanted to make the best goddamn Gears game we could. We wanted it to be a technical and art showpiece, and I think getting to see Asha on-stage say, 'To return to Xbox, we're returning to Gears,' yeah, that's a really cool moment.

He continued: "We know how much Xbox means to a lot of people. We're proud to be one of Xbox's main titles – I think it's been that way for a long time – and it's pretty cool to show up now and fill that role again."

Gears of War: E-Day launched in early access for Premium Edition players on PC and Xbox Series X/S October 1, 2026. Its full launch will follow this week, October 6. IGN's early review, which covered only the campaign mode, returned a 9/10 . The game's story director was laid off just one week before it made its way to players' hands a few days ago. Now, more developers at The Coalition is bracing for additional layoffs .

articles.title: Fourth RuneScape MMO Built With Unreal Engine in the Works, Jagex Announces RuneScape Animation With MoistCr1TiKaL
articles.summary: Developer Jagex has announced a fourth MMO in the long-running RuneScape franchise, as well as an animated adaptation.
articles.body:
Developer Jagex has announced a fourth MMO in the long-running RuneScape franchise, as well as an animated adaptation.

At RuneFest in Birmingham, England, Jagex offered a glimpse at this new MMO, which it said was built “for a new generation of players.” It’s still in early development (a release isn't expected for at least a few years), and it doesn’t have an official title (Jagex is going with RS4 as a working title for now), but it will “bring the world of Gielinor to life in Unreal Engine, combining the depth, freedom and community-led spirit that have defined RuneScape for 25 years with the technology and game design possibilities of today.”

Jagex currently operates RuneScape itself, Old School RuneScape, and spinoff RuneScape: Dragonwilds. RuneScape has seen a number of major updates tied to sequel names, including a rename to RuneScape 2 in 2004 and RuneScape 3 in 2013. But both were dropped in favor of, simply, RuneScape, and it is now treated as an ongoing live service. It's tempting, then, to call this new game RuneScape 4, and it may end up justifying the name, but Jagex has yet to rubber stamp any title.

Indeed, we hardly know anything about this new RuneScape MMO, but with the mention of Unreal Engine, the expectation is it will have modern visuals and design. An image from the concept teaser and the concept teaser itself are below.

Here's the official blurb on the fourth RuneScape MMO:

Headlining RuneFest was the first glimpse of an ambitious new chapter for RuneScape: a fourth RuneScape MMO, built for a new generation of players. Still early in development, the as-yet-unnamed title will bring the world of Gielinor to life in Unreal Engine, combining the depth, freedom and community-led spirit that have defined RuneScape for 25 years with the technology and game design possibilities of today.

In a blog post , Jagex explained that it has announced RuneScape 4 so early because it wants to build on the tech development it made for Dragonwilds, and lean on the community co-development it established through RuneScape and Old School. The developer insisted RS4 is not a replacement for either RuneScape, Old School, or Dragonwilds, each of which has its own dedicated team and will continue to see investment. "We’ll be designing RS4 to sit alongside them as an additional way to experience RuneScape and the world of Gielinor," Jagex said.

"In fact, we think having different RuneScape experiences can make the whole family stronger," the developer continued. "Players may spend most of their time in one game, move between several, or discover Gielinor for the very first time through RS4. The ambition isn't to replace the RuneScape games you love. It's to make the RuneScape universe bigger."

Jagex also confirmed RS4 will be set in Gielinor, as you'd expect, and in the Sixth Age. "But we're beginning somewhere that RuneScape players have only recently started to discover - and that is Ashenfall. An area first explored in RuneScape: Dragonwilds, and a landmass to the north-east of the Gielinor.

"RS4 will take place years after the events of Dragonwilds and the destruction of the Dragon Queen Kuldra. Time has passed, the world has moved on, and Ashenfall has changed with it. But Ashenfall is only the beginning.

"Our ambition is for this adventure to grow far beyond Ashenfall over time, moving into places you know and love, as well as opening up new places and stories across Gielinor."

RuneScape is of course one of the longest-running video games in the world. Jagex says it’s seen over 300 million player accounts created in the 25 years since RuneScape first launched. But the company’s plan is to expand the franchise into new genres and even adaptations. For example, at RuneFest Jagex also announced work had started on a new RuneScape animated adaption, in partnership with YouTuber Charlie White, aka MoistCr1TiKaL, and LA-based production company Lyrical Media. Here’s the official blurb:

Additionally, Jagex unveiled plans to expand RuneScape beyond games, partnering with creator and internet phenomenon, Charlie White aka MoistCr1TiKaL as well as acclaimed LA Based production business Lyrical Media, to bring the world, characters and stories of Gielinor to life in a new exciting animated adaption.

Jagex announced a lot more at RuneFest today. Here’s everything we saw .

articles.title: Everything We Saw at RuneFest 2026, Including RuneScape 4 and RuneScape Reignited
articles.summary: RuneFest 2026 is over, and we’ve got a roundup of everything announced at Jagex’s big show celebrating its long-running fantasy MMORPG.
articles.body:
RuneFest 2026 is over, and we’ve got a roundup of everything announced at Jagex’s big show celebrating its long-running fantasy MMORPG.

This year saw a number of significant announcements, none bigger than confirmation that a fourth RuneScape MMO is in the works . Jagex hasn’t officially called it RuneScape 4 (RS4 is the working title), but we know it’s built on Unreal Engine and is designed to use the latest technology and design, so it really does sound like a next-gen RuneScape game. There’s no information on when it will be released, but the teaser trailer is below.

Jagex announced a new RuneScape animated adaptation, in partnership with YouTuber Charlie White, aka MoistCr1TiKaL, and production company Lyrical Media. No word on what this is exactly or when it will be released, but it’s happening!

Jagex announced RuneScape Reignited, which launches December 2. Jagex called it a “defining moment” for the 25-year-old game, designed to rekindle interest among lapsed players and get existing players excited. There’s a Remastered Journey and Adventure Guide, a fresh economy, and brand-new hi scores. Players can get full Reignited Access without membership from December 2-12. The long-awaited Plugin API launches this month, with players getting an early hands-on ahead of official release. The debut trailer is below:

We also got what Jagex called “the biggest roadmap in the game’s history.” 2027 content unfolds in three story arcs, all of which tie into long-running storylines. Hoard of Dragons (January) offers a sequel to the popular Dragon Slayer quest, City of Gnomes continues the gnome storyline, and Secrets of Karamja introduces a new endgame raid. Also coming is an Agility skill rework, new skilling and solo bosses, new area expansions, and a new Grandmaster Quest.

Old School RuneScape, meanwhile, got an updated roadmap. The Golden Gates to Menaphos are opening finally after 20 years, alongside a suite of fan-demanded content. The Fractured Archive, a new endgame raid, launches October 20. Hardcore Worlds launches November 4. And next year will also see the continuation of the Fairytale questline, Quest month, Dungeons of Gielinor, a Mining and Smithing rework, Chosen Commander, and the Tower of Xorphoros.

The recently released spinoff, RuneScape: Dragonwilds, saw the announcement of the Blood Crystal Saga and updated plans for 2027. The Luminance update is a prelude to 2027’s Blood Crystal Saga, and launches in December this year. articles.title: Inde Navarrette Teases X-Men Role, Says She's 'Doing Everything Humanly Possible' to Do Rogue Justice
articles.summary: Inde Navarrette has opened up about playing Rogue in X-Men, saying she's "doing everything humanly possible" to make sure she does the character justice.
articles.body:
Inde Navarrette has opened up about playing Rogue in X-Men , saying she's "doing everything humanly possible" to make sure she does the character justice.

The Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) X-Men reboot movie has a lot to live up to. For better or worse, previous films in the mutant-centered corner of the Marvel universe spent decades establishing characters like Cyclops and Rogue, and now, Navarrette is one of a few actors set to shake everything up.

The actress, who was picked to play the power-siphoning superhero earlier this year, told the LA Times that she's not taking her role in the reboot lightly. In fact, she's doing anything but.

"I'm doing everything humanly possible because I love that character," Navarrette said. "I've studied that character. I want to do it justice for myself, for [director Jake Schrieier], for what they want to portray and also for what I as a fan want her to be like. I’m doing everything, exclamation point."

Having parts in shows like 13 Reasons Why and Superman & Lois means Navarrette has been on TV screens for years, but her role as Nikki in low-budget horror phenomenon Obsession took her fame to a new level. Through all of the Oscar buzz and turned-down parts , it was Schreier's X-Men she decided to sign on to for one of her first post-Obsession roles.

Playing Rogue in X-Men means stepping into the shoes of a character with decades of history. Aside from the Mississippi-born mutant's history in comics, she's also already appeared in numerous animated and live-action projects, with actress Anna Paquin portraying her in films like the 2000 X-Men movie and X2: X-Men United.

Meanwhile, Navarrette also recently teased some of the steps she's taking just to make sure she nails Rogue's unforgettable southern accent . While she preps for what could be the biggest role of her career, she's already got a few notable names in her corner. Last month, Lenore Zann, the voice of Rogue in multiple animated X-Men projects through the years, offered her support to the Marvel newcomer .

Navarette will take the reins – but not until 2028. The MCU X-Men Movie is currently slated to premiere May 5 of that year, and when it does, it will introduce a collection of other new actors to play familiar characters. The full list includes Navarrette as Rogue, Adam Driver as Mister Sinister, Maya Boyd as Storm, Christopher Abbott as Professor X, Sadie Sink as Jean Grey, Kit Connor as Cyclops, Samara Weaving as Emma Frost, and Asa Germann as Angel . Details about its plot remain under wraps, but Schreier has teased some of the comic book stories that will inspire its story .

In the meantime, some of the previous X-Men are set to return to the big screen when Avengers: Doomsday marks the beginning of the end for another MCU saga this December. With Avengers: Secret Wars set to arrive the following year , there's no telling which other heroes will make an appearance in the near future.

articles.title: Avengers: Doomsday Poster Highlights Doctor Doom and 3 Latverian Witches
articles.summary: Marvel Studios has revealed a new Avengers: Doomsday poster, giving audiences a closer look not only at Doctor Doom but also at the three Latverian witches who will accompany him this December.
articles.body:
Marvel Studios has revealed a new Avengers: Doomsday poster, giving audiences a closer look not only at Doctor Doom but also at the three Latverian witches who will accompany him this December.

This latest look at the new Marvel Cinematic Universe movie was shared on social media as part of this weekend's San Diego Comic-Con Málaga in Spain. It was an event that saw stars like Anthony Mackie, Winston Duke, and David Harbor make an appearance, with this latest look coming arriving as a little more than a high-res look at Robert Downey Jr.'s take on a classic comic book villain .

Doctor Doom takes center stage in the new Avengers: Doomsday poster. He's looking as menacing as ever, striking a pose similar to the one we've seen before but with somewhat better lighting. The real highlight from the new poster, however, is the three Latverian witches standing behind him.

These three witches – and their hidden identities – have been the subject of much debate amongst MCU fans the last few months. These same mystery characters brought their purple, red, and green robes to San Diego Comic-Con in California this past July. The average onlooker might assume these characters will be little more than henchmen to be discarded in a massive CGI fight sequence, but some aren't so convinced.

Warning! Potential Avengers: Doomsday spoilers follow.

Many believe the faces behind these cold metal masks may be ones we've seen before. Prominent theories suspect the witch with the red robes could be Elizabeth Olsen's Wanda Maximoff, with the green-robed witch's secret identity being Loki show alum Sophia Di Martino's Sylvie.

While not everyone has landed on the same answer for these aforementioned witches, fans are truly split when it comes to who the character wearing the purple robe is. Some say it's Kathryn Hahn's Agatha Harkness, while others believe it's Charlize Theron's Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness cameo character, Clea.

Hot Toys Avengers: Doomsday Victor von Doom Figure

As these are all just theories for now, there's always the chance all three Latverian witches could be nothing more than Doom drones for the Avengers to fight through. Still, recent developments in the MCU have led some to believe Avengers: Doomsday has some secret cameos it's saving for theaters.

Meanwhile, Mackie took his Comic-Con appearance as an opportunity to tease some of the most surprising moments from the new movie. X/Twitter user @CatherineComTH captured and shared the moment online.

"I think the big thing is the amount of doom you're going to see," he said when asked what people will be most surprised by. "Every corner we turn and every time somebody speaks, it's like, 'There's a lot of doom outside.' It's non-stop pandemonium.

"The best part about that is what the Russo brothers are great at: giving every character and every person their moment. Every time I go to watch Endgame, every single character was given their moment for the audience to connect with them and grieve with them. I think it's the same in this movie. You just have so many people."

All will be revealed when Avengers: Doomsday arrives December 18, 2026. Until then, you can see what directors Joe and Anthony Russo had to say about the film's runtime . You can also read what Nightcrawler actor Alan Cumming said regarding his lack of understanding of the movie's plot .
